summary: The held PR767 DOM source passed its pure controls and never ran. Its template-package control replaced `dotnet` with a fake that asserted the argument `--package`; the real SDK 10.0.401 rejects that option (exit 127), so the receiver could never have been generated. A second gap was invisible to every pure control: the typed selection reached only the build, not the separate Playwright processes, so four opt-in specs registered no case (5 of 9 identities listed). Both surfaced only on the first real execution under ADR-0096 ordinary local verification. Practice: when a pure control stands in for a tool, assert what the real tool accepts (or run the real tool once in a fresh private root) rather than asserting the shape of the call that the fake was written to receive; derive cross-process inputs from one typed source and assert every consumer process receives them; and prefer one cheap real execution to additional fakes. A mutation that restores the old behavior must fail the control. This records an observation from one lane, not a rule for every test; fakes remain right for unreachable effects.
title: A control that fakes the exact boundary it checks proves nothing about that boundary
